title: Up in Order, Down in Reverse: Bringing a Graph of Nodes Up and Rolling It Back

questions.question: Why not start every node at once and let them find each other?
options: Starting them all at once uses too much memory at start up
The bus cannot register more than one node at a time
Nodes started together get the same incarnation number
The robot works when the machine is fast and fails when it is not, and when one node does not come up the others are left running without it
questions.explanation: A node that starts before what it needs may or may not cope, depending on how fast the machine is that day. An order worked out from the needs does not depend on luck.

questions.question: Planner, controller, filter, driver, logger and viewer are listed in that order, each needing the one it follows in the chain. What is the start order?
options: driver filter planner controller logger viewer: every node after what it needs, ties going to the one listed first
planner controller filter driver logger viewer, as listed
controller driver filter logger planner viewer, alphabetical
viewer logger controller planner filter driver, the reverse of the needs
questions.explanation: The driver needs nothing, the filter needs the driver, and so on up. Among nodes that could go next, the one listed first goes.

questions.question: What does a circle of needs do to the start order?
options: The list is refused with the reason: a needing b needing c needing a has no start order
The nodes are started in the order listed, and the circle is ignored
The first node in the circle is started and the others wait for it
They are all started together, since none can go first
questions.explanation: No order can put each of three nodes after the one it needs when the needs go round. The list is refused and the reason given.

questions.question: Why configure every node before activating any?
options: Activating is slower than configuring, so it is done last
The bus needs every topic to exist before any message is sent
So that the nodes can be activated in any order
Nothing produces until it is known that everything which consumes it exists, so a failed configure has not yet sent a single message
questions.explanation: Configuring is where devices are opened and things fail. Doing all of it first means that a failure is found before anything has started producing.

questions.question: The planner will not configure. What does the log show?
options: planner:configure and nothing else: the failure is found before anything is touched
driver:configure filter:configure planner:configure driver:activate filter:activate: what could run was started
driver:configure filter:configure planner:configure filter:cleanup driver:cleanup: the ones that did configure are cleaned up in reverse and nothing was activated
driver:configure filter:configure planner:configure planner:cleanup: only the one that failed is cleaned up
questions.explanation: The planner is required, so the bring up stops. The filter and the driver had configured and are undone, newest first.

questions.question: An optional logger fails and a plotter needs it. What is running?
options: Nothing: any failure stops the bring up
Driver, filter and controller: logger and plotter are left out, and the report says which were skipped
Driver, filter, controller and plotter: only the logger is left out
Everything, with the logger marked as failed
questions.explanation: An optional node's failure is not worth the robot. What needed it cannot run either, and the report names both.
